title: Times −1 on both sides
hook: An equation stays true when you do the same to both sides. What about 2 < 5?

knows: negative numbers on a number line
doesNotKnow: why multiplying both sides of an inequality by a negative number flips the sign while adding or multiplying by a positive keeps it

misconception: An inequality behaves like an equation: do the same to both sides and it stays true as written, so 2 < 5 gives −2 < −5.
objective: The learner can explain that multiplying both sides of an inequality by a negative number mirrors the number line through 0, which swaps left and right and so flips the sign.

claims.text: Times 2 sends 2 and 5 to 4 and 10 (4 < 10); minus 3 sends them to −1 and 2 (−1 < 2); times −2 sends them to −4 and −10 (−4 > −10).
claims.source: Check A4 (x2 4 10 <; -3 -1 2 <; x-2 -4 -10 >). The reveal quotes the first order-keeping chip the learner pressed, recorded when the 'kept' milestone fires.
claims.note: Arithmetic: x2 gives 4 < 10; -3 gives -1 < 2; x(-2) gives -4 > -10 (re-run). The number line runs -10..10, so every endpoint fits.

claims.text: If a < b, then a + c < b + c for every c, ac < bc when c > 0, and ac > bc when c < 0: adding, subtracting or multiplying by a positive keeps the order, multiplying by a negative flips it.
claims.source: b − a > 0, so (b − a)c > 0 when c > 0 and (b − a)c < 0 when c < 0; (b + c) − (a + c) = b − a > 0.
claims.note: Derivation: (b + c) - (a + c) = b - a > 0; (b - a)c has the sign of c.

claims.text: Multiplying by −1 mirrors the number line through 0, and a mirror swaps left and right.
claims.source: x ↦ −x sends each point to the point the same distance from 0 on the other side (a reflection), and reverses order: a < b implies −a > −b.
claims.note: Derivation: x -> -x is the reflection through 0 and reverses order. The stage also draws 'mirror' for x(-2), which is a mirror plus a stretch; the reveal's 'Multiplying by a negative mirrors the line' is right for the order, which is the point. Recall (-3 < 4 divided by -1 gives 3 > -4) checks out.

claims.text: An equation stays true when you do the same thing to both sides (add, subtract, multiply).
claims.source: If a = b then a + c = b + c and ac = bc (substitution of equals).
claims.note: Derivation: substitution of equals (if a = b then a + c = b + c and ac = bc).

recall.question: −3 < 4. Divide both sides by −1. Which is true?
recall.why: Dividing by −1 is the same as multiplying by −1: it mirrors the line through 0, so the order swaps. 3 is to the right of −4, so 3 > −4.
